title: The project profile, .ai-kit.yaml at the git top level (KIT-087)
description: Project-owned parameters that only the kit reads: its skills, hooks, sync-project.sh and the spec-tools action, through platforms/tools/profile.py. Every key has a default and one reader phase (x-read-by: session, sdd, implement, review, delivery, security). A key the project does not set takes the value its project.kind preset gives (project.kind x-presets), else its default (KIT-088). Unknown keys fail; x-<name> keys, at the top level or directly in a section, are the project's and the kit ignores them.

^x-.description: Project-private key: the kit accepts and ignores it (KIT-087)

kit.description: Compatibility pin: the lowest kit version this profile needs, e.g. '>=15'; null = any

project.description: What kind of project this is (KIT-088); only the resolver reads it

^x-.description: Project-private key: the kit accepts and ignores it (KIT-087)

kind.description: A preset of defaults that no skill reads: a key the project does not set takes the value x-presets gives for this kind, else its schema default. business: every schema default; game: the four game vision sections, the Assets Plan section, greybox and polish passes, playtest acceptance, owner visual approval; tooling: the FEAT-only flow of a tool repository (no NEED, no REQ, no task table, one PR per FEAT, a record for a big change only, Tests and Risks Plan sections, manual release)

spec_root.description: The folder that holds the SDD spec (spec.md, needs/, features/, journeys/ ...), relative to the git top level (KIT-088): folder names of letters, digits, dot, underscore and hyphen joined by single slashes, with no . or .. segment and no backslash (KIT-087 P2a); the resolver fails when the folder resolves outside the root

stacks.description: Folder ('.' for the root) -> its stack, or a list of stacks; selects the kit rules (sync-project.sh, the path-rule hook) and the stack recipes

^x-.description: Project-private key: the kit accepts and ignores it (KIT-087)

sdd.description: The SDD process parameters (KIT-067): the keys spec.md's sdd: block held until KIT-087 P4 (less review_rounds and visual_approval, now review.rounds and evidence.visual_approval), plus task_cut and decision_folding (KIT-086) and vision_sections, passes, acceptance, flow, task_table, record_when, id_prefix (KIT-088) and migrations (KIT-095); sdd-constitution/references/sdd-parameters.md names each reader

needs.description: NEED-nnn intake records under docs/spec/needs/; read by sdd-intake, sdd-specify, sdd-clarify

journeys.description: J-nn journeys under docs/spec/journeys/; read by sdd-clarify, sdd-check, sync-project.sh; absent = on when the folder exists; null (the default) = on when docs/spec/journeys/ exists

tracker.description: Where task rows are cut: GitHub issues, or none (task files in the repository); read by sdd-tasks, sdd-implement, sdd-spike

plan_sections.description: The FEAT ## Plan subsections this project fills; Risks and Tests are always on; read by sdd-plan

pr_unit.description: One PR per task row or one per FEAT; read by sdd-implement

task_minutes.description: Upper size of a task row for one fresh agent context, in minutes; read by sdd-tasks

row_check.description: Project command that checks the task rows before the cut; null = the kit row checks (row_checks.py, KIT-073); read by sdd-tasks

cut_command.description: Project command that cuts the approved rows; null = the kit cut; read by sdd-tasks

max_chain.description: Longest dependency chain allowed among a FEAT's task rows; read by sdd-tasks

max_feat_tasks.description: Task rows above which a FEAT is too large for one delivery: check_spec.py warns and sdd-plan splits the NEED into several FEATs; read by sdd-plan, sdd-tasks

release.description: merge: a FEAT is delivered once its work is on main (after its sdd-review closure, KIT-069); manual: sdd-release delivers it; read by sdd-review, sdd-release

commits_by.description: Who commits a task's work: the executor session or the orchestrator; read by sdd-implement

protected_paths.description: Path or glob -> label a change to it needs; read by sdd-tasks and review

bundle.description: Limits for one issue that bundles task rows sharing a Files path; rows 1 = one issue per row; read by sdd-tasks

points.description: Sum of the rows' Complexity, Low 1, Med 2, High 3

rule_paths.description: Kit rule name -> folders its globs are scoped to, '.' for the whole repository; wins over the --profile folders; read by sync-project.sh

components.description: Component name -> its folder in this repository, '.' for the root: a Files entry or test path may start with either; one task row stays in one component. Read by row_checks.py (rules b, c, e, g, i, j, k) and spec_trace.py (journey test paths)

spec_index.description: spec_trace.py check fails when docs/spec/spec.md lacks a linked table row for a functional or non-functional REQ file or a journey file, or links a missing one

github.description: Where spec_trace.py sync-status reads task issues and their PRs (tracker: github only)

repo.description: owner/name of the backlog repository that holds the task issues; null = the origin remote

pr_repos.description: Other owner/name repositories whose PRs close backlog issues

aliases.description: Earlier owner/name names of the backlog repository that a Closes line may still use

blocked_labels.description: Issue labels that make a row blocked

progress_labels.description: Issue labels that make a row doing without an open PR

row_checks.description: Inputs of the kit row checks (row_checks.py, KIT-073); a rule whose input is null or empty is off; sdd-tasks/references/row-checks.md names each rule

gates.description: Repository path of the PR gates JSON (pr_gates.py): proof_allowlist, proof_script_runners, generated_neighbours (rules d, e, g)

tests.description: Rule c, per stack: a Files entry matching a code glob (minus exclude) needs an entry matching or covering the tests glob ($1.. are the code glob's wildcards); level fail or warn

assets.description: Rule d: an exact Files path under paths ending in one of suffixes needs a covering directory glob

protocol.description: Rules h and k: the contract folder, the message schema folder (<type>.json) and each consumer's generated tables

evidence_only.description: Rule e: true lets a row whose Proof holds only evidence: clauses pass with no runnable clause; false fails it (KIT-080)

artifacts.description: Rule i: repository path of the artifact policy registry, a JSON list of {pattern, dec, policy}

visual.description: Rule j (with visual_approval owner or reviewer): Files paths that change a screen or motion, paths to ignore, and the evidence catalog file per kind ($id)

owner_approvals.description: Change kinds only the owner may approve, for example decision, approved-dec-change, protocol-version, in-game-evidence; read by review (KIT-069) and an orchestrator session under owner-review autonomy

doc_structure.description: The README and done/INDEX.md check (check_docs_structure.py, KIT-074), opt-in; read by the check itself, which the docs just module and the spec-tools action run

enabled.description: Run the check: just lint and the spec-tools action run the kit's check_docs_structure.py, which passes as off while false

exempt.description: File of fnmatch globs (one per line, from the repository root) for folders a parent README covers

headings.description: Headings every folder README carries after its # title

done_index.description: Every done/ folder has an INDEX.md naming each direct child

task_cut.description: The task cut checklist parameters KIT-086 moves into sdd-tasks; read by sdd-tasks

owned_area_form.description: How a row's Files cell names an owned area: paths (exact files and folders) or globs

required_test_folders.description: Code glob -> the test folders a row touching it must also list

bundle_exclude.description: Globs a bundled item never shares: each such row is its own item

longest_chain_max_complexity.description: Highest Complexity a row on a FEAT's longest Depends on chain may carry; default Med, the kit's rule before the key (waves-and-models.md); High = no limit

decision_folding.description: How a decision is folded into the specs and task status (KIT-086); read by sdd-plan and sdd-tasks

marker.description: The text that marks a decision folded into a spec

vision_sections.description: The optional spec.md sections this project writes besides the template's own (Vision, First-delivery scope, Out of scope, Glossary, Architecture), by heading text, e.g. Pillars, Core loop, Direction, References; [] = none; read by sdd-constitution

passes.description: The passes a new mechanic's FEAT is planned in, in this order: greybox (playable, placeholder art), then polish, cut after the greybox playtest; [] = one pass; read by sdd-plan, sdd-tasks, sdd-review, sdd-check C16, and review and row_checks.py rule j, which exempt a greybox block's rows from visual approval (KIT-094)

acceptance.description: What accepts a delivered FEAT: captures (the captures visual_approval names, the step before this key) or playtest (a playtest record the owner signs); read by sdd-review, sdd-release

flow.description: full: NEED, REQ, FEAT and task rows; feat-only: a FEAT holds its rules in its acceptance criteria, sdd-clarify is skipped and a FEAT needs no REQ (KIT-100); read by sdd-clarify, sdd-check, sdd-plan, sdd-review

task_table.description: false: a FEAT carries no ## Tasks table and is itself the item (one issue, one PR); read by sdd-tasks

record_when.description: always: every change gets its FEAT; big-change: only a big change does, and any other change needs only its changelog line and its PR body's why; read by sdd-plan

id_prefix.description: The id prefix of a spec artifact kind (KIT-088)

feature.description: The FEAT id prefix, e.g. KIT for KIT-NNN records; read by sdd-plan, check_spec.py, spec_trace.py

migrations.description: Folders of schema migrations, rooted at the repository, whose every file an ENB catalog row (Schema or file) must cover: spec_trace.py enablers walks each as <folder>/**/* for C19, as it walks row_checks.protocol.schemas; [] = none (KIT-095, KIT-087 P2b)
